tagline: Design a randomised experiment a public office can act on, size it, check it and read its result without fooling yourself
description: Participants design randomised experiments for a fictional municipal permits office and read the results without fooling themselves. They turn a decision question into a pre-registration with a hypothesis, primary and guardrail metrics, a stop rule and a unit of randomisation, compute sample size by formula and by simulation, analyse a synthetic experiment log, check that randomisation worked, and measure how peeking, many metrics and a mismatched unit inflate false wins. Variance reduction and sequential tests are left to DS-302.
audience: Practitioners. Graduates and early-career analysts who have completed the FN courses or passed the placement test, and analysts moving into data science.
prerequisites: Computes a proportion, a difference in means and a confidence interval
Writes a simulation loop in Python or R
Pre-work: about two hours on proportions, intervals and simulation, in the pre-work notebook of the labs folder (its name starts with P0), before the supervised entry quiz
Setup: a laptop with uv, or Google Colab. Nothing calls or downloads a model. Run 00_setup_check before Day 1; see labs/README.md.

outcomes.text: Distinguish a randomised experiment, a quasi-experiment and an observational comparison, and explain the causal claim each supports, given six study descriptions from public services
outcomes.evidence: a classification with the supported claim, at least five of six correct

outcomes.text: Draft a pre-registration stating the decision, hypothesis, unit of randomisation, primary and guardrail metrics, stop rule and analysis plan, given the office's question about renewal reminders
outcomes.evidence: a one-page pre-registration that passes a reviewer's checklist

outcomes.text: Compute the sample size and run time needed to detect a minimum effect of interest and check it by simulation, given baseline renewal rates, daily traffic and the office's minimum effect
outcomes.evidence: a notebook with the formula result, a simulated power curve and the chosen duration

outcomes.text: Analyse a completed two-arm experiment with a difference in proportions, a confidence interval and a sample ratio mismatch test, given a synthetic log of 60,000 renewal notices
outcomes.evidence: a result note with estimate, interval, checks and a recommendation

outcomes.text: Measure by simulation the false-positive rate caused by peeking, many metrics and analysis at the wrong unit, given simulated A/A tests with no true effect
outcomes.evidence: a table of false-win rates for each trap, with and without the correct procedure

outcomes.text: Review a reported experiment and decide whether it supports the decision it claims to support, given write-ups with seeded flaws, one in class and one in the capstone
outcomes.evidence: a review memo per write-up naming each flaw, its consequence and the decision the evidence does support, defended live

case_study.name: Mashraq Municipal Permits Office
case_study.summary: Mashraq Municipal Permits Office (مكتب المشرق للتصاريح البلدية) is a fictional city office that issues resident parking, market stall, outdoor seating and building works permits. Its director, Sahar Al-Wuhaibi, wants three changes tested before they are adopted: a reminder message for renewals, a redesigned online form and a new way of serving visitors at the counters of 24 branches. All data are synthetic and generated with a fixed seed: 26 weeks of notice traffic with a weekly cycle and a month-end peak, a reminder test on 60,000 notices over 28 days whose platform export has a planted fault, a form test logged page view by page view, and four baseline weeks of counter visits in branches of which three pairs share staff. Participants work as Juri Al-Asmari, a junior analyst; holders, applicants and visitors appear only as pseudonymised keys and every result is reported in aggregate.

format_note: Intensive: 3 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task

days.title: Capstone: the design and analysis pack and its defence
days.subtitle: Each participant defends one design choice of a pack on one of three synthetic cases in eight minutes, then answers four minutes of questions

capstone.summary: A design and analysis pack for one of three synthetic cases (reminder message, form redesign, training programme): pre-registration, sample-size and analysis notebooks, result note and a review memo on a flawed write-up, in a public repository; eight-minute defence
capstone.submission: A link to a public GitHub repository with a one-page pre-registration, a sample-size notebook with the formula result and a simulated power curve, an analysis notebook that reruns from the raw files with a fixed seed, a result note with estimate, interval, checks and a recommendation, and a review memo on the case's flawed write-up, with the commit history and the seeded simulation log. Then an eight-minute live defence of one design choice and four minutes of questions, in which the assessor changes the minimum effect or the unit and the participant recomputes the sample size.
